scope: High-priority claim-level photoperiod and daily-photon evidence for THC-ENC-104.
rules: Photoperiod flowering responses remain bounded to tested germplasm, propagation material, environments, light schedules, and flowering definitions.
A daily photon integral does not preserve dark duration, photon rate, spectrum, circadian timing, or cultivar-specific flowering response.
Meta-analytic timing estimates describe the included literature and must not be converted into universal cultivar schedules.
All mappings remain pending independent science review and do not alter lesson publication or independent-approval state.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cannabis/hemp flowering and production responses depend on photoperiod timing and germplasm; experiments show cultivar-specific critical-photoperiod behavior and a synthesis of indoor studies links vegetative long-day duration with differing floral-biomass and cannabinoid outcomes, so equal daily photon totals cannot be assumed biologically equivalent across schedules.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: Zhang et al. (2021), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.694153; Dang, Muthu Arachchige, and Campbell (2022), DOI 10.3389/fpls.2021.797425.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson's distinction between integrated photon dose and developmental light-dark timing, including cultivar dependence and the need to record actual photoperiod transitions.
claimEvidence.limitations: Zhang et al. tested specific essential-oil, fiber, and grain hemp cultivars; Dang et al. synthesized heterogeneous published studies. Neither establishes a universal critical photoperiod, flowering schedule, DLI equivalence rule, or cultivar-independent optimum.
